in_hebrew.name: ברטולומאו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם בשמות, היוצר והגנה, כפי שמתאר הפסוק "כי-שומר ישראל" (שמות ו, 21). בתלמוד (סנהדרין, ד, 23) מוזכר "שומר" (שומר, 'watcher'') ו'בר' (בנו, 'son of') שם, פעמים רבות.

in_greek.name: Ματθαῖος
in_greek.long_meaning: השם 'Ματθαῖος' בערבית 'Bartolomeo', מקורו בשם העברי 'משמר', 'watcher' (שמות, 5:2) ו'אח' (אח, 'brother').

in_latin.name: Bartolomeo
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Bartolomeo derivatur a nomine Hebraico 'Bar', 'filius' et 'Tolomeo', 'defensor'. In historia ecclesiastica Bartolomeo erat discipulus apostolorum et nunc sanctus martyr.

in_english.name: Bartolomeo
in_english.meaning: defender, protector, or guardian, a name derived from Hebrew roots
in_english.long_meaning: The name Bartolomeo is derived from the Hebrew roots 'Bar', meaning 'son of', and 'Tolomeo', meaning 'defender'. In Christian tradition, Saint Bartholomew was one of Jesus' twelve apostles and is now revered as a saint and martyr. This name carries the spiritual significance of protection, guardianship, and defense, reflecting the qualities of a steadfast and loyal individual.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bartolomeo originated from the Aramaic term "Bar Toma," which means "Son of Thunder," and was given to St. Bartholomew, one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus Christ. In the Christian tradition, St. Bartolomeo is associated with perfume makers and leatherworkers. He is also regarded as the patron saint of butchers, winegrowers, and against herds of pigs. Interestingly, it was believed that St. Bartholomeo was martyred by being flayed alive, making his memorial day on August 24 an important feast day.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bartolomeo carries a powerful spiritual significance, reminding us of the call of St. Bartholomeo to ministry by seeing Christ in the form of an angel. It also symbolizes the spiritual journey of each individual, highlighting the importance of recognizing and responding to God's call, no matter how unexpected or challenging it may be. The name Bartolomeo can serve as a constant reminder to seek the will of God in all aspects of life and to respond with faith, trust, and courage.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bartolomeo, meaning "tillable land" in Aramaic, symbolizes the fertile ground of one's soul, prepared for the seed of faith to take root and grow. Spiritually, it represents the call to cultivate one's inner self, allowing the Word of God to nurture and transform it.
